newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale says grain delays due to locomotive supply.
newsitem.headline: Goodale says grain delays due to locomotive supply.

text.p: A shortage of railroad locomotives is to blame for 43 ships waiting to load grains and oilseeds at Canadian Pacific ports this week and will be the focus of a meeting of the grain and rail industries called by Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale.

"Locomotive power in the fleet seems to be undersupplied and those two factors have put the whole system way behind putting the grain through the Rockies," Goodale told reporters in Ottawa, referring to a locomotive shortage and bad weather.
On Tuesday 43 ocean vessels were waiting to load grain on the Pacific coast, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Sixteen of those ships were destined for Japan, 12 waited to load CWB wheat and barley while three waited for canola and one for oats. The longest wait was for 40 days, the CWB said.
Cold weather accompanied by heavy snow and sporadic Prairie elevator grain deliveries were blamed by some railway companies for the delay.
The CWB, grain and transportation analysts said grain shipments were a lower priority for the railways since they generate lower profits versus some other commodities.
Rail rates on grain cannot exceed a federally-imposed cap while other commodities may get priority because of premiums.
